If the parent closes or a pushable -- frame overlaps them they must be hidden."). Dropped as "none exist yet" until 1507 — -- all four ship now: the open letter (MailFrame.xml) and the guild pane's three -- satellites (FriendsFrame.xml). The parent-close half is each parent's own OnHide -- (MailFrame hides the letter, FriendsFrame_OnHide hides the satellites); this table -- serves the OVERLAP half — SetCenterFrame's hide loop below — because the child popups -- sit exactly where the center seat puts a window. -- The real client stores `.left`/`.center`/`.doublewide`/`.fullscreen` as fields directly on -- the `UIParent` frame table (UIParent.lua l.789-885). benilla has no `UIParent` frame object -- yet (a later decision's job) — so the two slots this v1 tracks live in a private chunk-local -- table instead of squatting the `UIParent` global name; a future `CreateFrame("Frame", -- "UIParent")` then lands cleanly on an empty global rather than silently coexisting with our -- state. Every function below is defined in this same chunk, so they all close over it. local slots = { left = nil, center = nil, fullscreen = nil, doublewide = nil }
-- SetLeftFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.809-824. Hides the old left occupant, SetPoints + -- Shows the new one at the left slot's screen anchor (verified: TOPLEFT UIParent, 0, -104). -- "UIParent" as the relativeTo name doesn't resolve to a real frame yet (none exists) — the -- engine's SetPoint falls back to the frame's own parent-or-screen default, which for our -- top-level panel frames IS the screen root, so this already anchors correctly; the string is -- kept for fidelity/forward-compat with the day a real UIParent frame lands. function SetLeftFrame(frame) local oldFrame = slots.left slots.left = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) frame:Show() end end
-- SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) — UIParent.lua l.826-850, the `UIChildWindows` hide -- loop (l.839-846) carried since 1507: a frame ARRIVING at the center seat lands exactly -- where the child popups sit, so they are put away first. Arriving is the ref's exact -- trigger — MovePanelToCenter's slide re-seats by direct assignment after a -- SetCenterFrame(nil), so a PUSHED panel does not run the loop; kept as transcribed. -- (The ref's `for index, value in UIChildWindows do` is Lua 5.0's iterator-less -- generic-for, which our VM cannot run — decision 1202; `ipairs` is the same walk.) function SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) local oldFrame = slots.center slots.center = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:Show() if not skipSetPoint then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) end for _, name in ipairs(UIChildWindows) do local childWindow = getglobal(name) if childWindow then childWindow:Hide() end end end end
-- MovePanelToLeft() — UIParent.lua l.868-875: the center occupant slides back to the left slot -- (used when the left slot vacates and a "left-area" frame is holding center). function MovePanelToLeft() if slots.center then SetLeftFrame(nil) slots.center:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) slots.left = slots.center slots.center = nil end end
-- MovePanelToCenter() — UIParent.lua l.877-885: the left occupant slides to the center slot -- (used when a higher-`pushable` frame wants the left spot). `:Raise()` (l.881) has no benilla -- frame-level equivalent yet — guarded, same posture as the pin's `UnitIsDead` guard below. function MovePanelToCenter() if slots.left then SetCenterFrame(nil) slots.left:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) if slots.left.Raise then slots.left:Raise() end slots.center = slots.left slots.left = nil end end
-- GetLeftFrame / GetCenterFrame — UIParent.lua l.916-922. function GetLeftFrame() return slots.left end
function GetCenterFrame() return slots.center end
-- SetFullScreenFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.852-866. ONE line dropped: the reference also -- does `UIParent:Hide()`/`:Show()` around the swap, hiding the whole game UI behind the -- fullscreen frame. benilla has no UIParent frame (the note on `slots` above), and the only -- full frame we ship — the world map — already paints its own full-screen blackout -- (WorldMapFrame.xml), which is what that Hide buys the reference. function SetFullScreenFrame(frame) local oldFrame = slots.fullscreen slots.fullscreen = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:Show() end end
function GetFullScreenFrame() return slots.fullscreen end
-- SetDoublewideFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.788-808. One frame takes the left AND center -- seats at once: both incumbents are dropped (nil'd first, then hidden — the order matters, -- since an OnHide that re-enters this manager must not find itself still seated), and the -- new frame lands at the left slot's own screen anchor, because a doublewide window simply -- starts where left starts and is wide enough to cover both. -- -- Note what the reference does NOT do: `HideUIPanel` has no doublewide branch (l.754-786), -- so nothing ever clears this seat — `UIParent.doublewide` keeps pointing at the auction -- window forever once it has been opened, and every later ShowUIPanel re-hides an -- already-hidden frame. We reproduce that rather than inventing a clear: `Hide()` on a -- hidden frame fires nothing, so the difference is unobservable, and a "fix" here would be -- a silent divergence in the one function every window's placement runs through. function SetDoublewideFrame(frame) local oldLeft = slots.left local oldCenter = slots.center slots.doublewide = frame slots.left = nil slots.center = nil if oldLeft then oldLeft:Hide() end if oldCenter then oldCenter:Hide() end if frame then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) frame:Show() end end
-- GetDoublewideFrame — UIParent.lua l.924-926. function GetDoublewideFrame() return slots.doublewide end
-- The area a frame is REGISTERED for — or nil, which is equally the answer for no frame at -- all and for a frame this manager has never heard of. Four rules below turn on exactly -- that question ("is a native-center window holding the screen?", "is the frame parked at -- center a left-area one that should slide back?"), and all four want an absent frame and -- an unregistered one to answer the same way. The reference open-codes the pair of nil -- checks at each site, which is four chances to leave one of them out. local function AreaOf(frame) local info = frame and UIPanelWindows[frame:GetName()] return info and info.area end
-- CanOpenPanels() — UIParent.lua l.887-910. Its dead-player arms are commented out in the -- reference itself (both of them, with the note that the fear/out-of-control gate was -- "previously"); what survives is one rule: **a native-center frame open ⇒ nothing else -- opens**. The game menu is the only such frame (decision 0674), so this reads: with the -- ESC menu up, no window opens — not from a keybind, not from an NPC's OPEN_WINDOW. function CanOpenPanels() if AreaOf(GetCenterFrame()) == "center" then return nil end return 1 end
-- Everything that can REFUSE an open, asked in the reference's own order (UIParent.lua -- l.663-689). Answers false when the frame must not open. Not a pure predicate, and that -- is the point: `force` is precisely the right to throw the incumbent out instead of being -- turned away, so each refusal and its eviction are one decision and are written as one. local function AdmitPanel(info, force) -- A dead player gets only the windows that asked for it (l.663-666) — and hears why: -- NotWhileDeadError is the binary's 0x48d340 (wow-re §5 cross-check, 2026-08-21 — -- decision 1507's open item): push id 0x7e into the message catalog, whose row is -- ERR_PLAYER_DEAD → UI_ERROR_MESSAGE, sound "NONE". Our binding (ui_errors.rs) -- pushes the same key onto the engine's client-local error queue, which the app -- resolves against GlobalStrings and fires as the same event. The binding is a pure -- display trigger — this line, like the reference's, decides WHEN. if UnitIsDead("player") and not info.whileDead then NotWhileDeadError() return false end -- l.668-675: nothing opens behind a full-screen frame. The world map is the only -- `full` row we register, so this reads: nothing opens behind the map. if GetFullScreenFrame() and info.area ~= "full" then if not force then return false end SetFullScreenFrame(nil) end -- l.677-689: with a native-center frame open, only another center request gets -- through. Redundant with the caller's CanOpenPanels gate for anything that doesn't -- force (the reference double-checks it too); kept because it is the ONLY path that -- can displace the menu, and dropping it would silently turn `force` into a no-op. -- No benilla caller passes `force` yet. if AreaOf(GetCenterFrame()) == "center" and info.area ~= "center" then if not force then return false end SetCenterFrame(nil) end return true end
-- Seating a **left-area** panel (l.719-751). The left slot is what it wants; `pushable` -- settles what happens to whoever is already sitting there. Read the comparisons as "the -- higher number is the one that gets moved along" — and two zeroes will not move for each -- other at all, which is what makes one NPC window replace another outright. local function SeatLeftAreaPanel(frame, info) local leftFrame = GetLeftFrame() if not leftFrame then SetLeftFrame(frame) return end
local leftInfo = UIPanelWindows[leftFrame:GetName()] local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if centerFrame then -- Both seats taken (l.744-751): outrank the center occupant and it slides back to -- the left while we take center; otherwise settle for replacing the left one. if info.pushable > UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()].pushable then MovePanelToLeft() SetCenterFrame(frame) else SetLeftFrame(frame) end elseif leftInfo.pushable == 0 and info.pushable == 0 then -- Neither will budge — two NPC sessions — so we replace it outright (l.729-732, -- the gossip<->merchant case). SetLeftFrame(frame) elseif leftInfo.pushable > info.pushable then -- The incumbent outranks us, so it is promoted to center and we take the left slot -- it vacates (l.735-741 — highest priority goes to center). MovePanelToCenter() SetLeftFrame(frame) else SetCenterFrame(frame) end end
-- ShowUIPanel(frame) — UIParent.lua l.649-751, now the WHOLE slice: left, center, full -- and doublewide (pin §3 steps 1,3-5, plus the native-center mode decision 0674 needed and -- the `full` slot the world map took in 0203/0674). `doublewide` (l.706-716) arrived with -- the auction house, decision 1511 — the last arm below is now genuinely unreachable for a -- registered row and stays only as the defensive fallback its comment says it is. -- -- Two questions, in order: may it open at all, and where does it sit. function ShowUIPanel(frame, force) if not frame or frame:IsVisible() then return end
local info = UIPanelWindows[frame:GetName()] -- l.655-657. Note the reference's own precedence: an UNREGISTERED frame is not gated -- (the `info and` term), so a bare toplevel still shows with the menu up. The gate is -- asked unconditionally, because addons replace CanOpenPanels and expect to be asked. local panelsAllowed = CanOpenPanels() if not panelsAllowed and info and info.area ~= "center" then return end if not info then frame:Show() return end if not AdmitPanel(info, force) then return end
if info.area == "full" then -- l.692-696: full-screen frames just replace each other, and they take everything -- else with them on the way in. CloseAllWindows() SetFullScreenFrame(frame) elseif info.area == "center" then -- l.697-702: native-center frames likewise replace each other and take the -- screen. `skipSetPoint` is the load-bearing argument here — the menu keeps its -- own CENTER anchor instead of being dropped at the left-area seat. CloseWindows() CloseAllBags() SetCenterFrame(frame, 1) elseif info.area == "doublewide" then -- l.706-710: it wants both seats, so it takes both and nothing else is consulted -- — including its own `pushable`, which is why the auction house's registered 0 -- never means anything. SetDoublewideFrame(frame) elseif info.area == "left" then -- l.712-716: a doublewide incumbent is squatting the seat we are about to use, so -- it goes first. In the reference this is a bare statement between the branches -- rather than part of one, but every earlier arm has already returned by then, so -- the LEFT path is the only one that reaches it — which is why it lives here. And -- since `HideUIPanel` never clears the slot, this is a plain Hide of a frame that -- may well already be hidden — see SetDoublewideFrame's note. local doublewide = GetDoublewideFrame() if doublewide then doublewide:Hide() end SeatLeftAreaPanel(frame, info) else -- An area string this manager does not know: defensive fallback only. frame:Show() end end
-- HideUIPanel(frame) — UIParent.lua l.754-786. Which seat is the frame sitting in? That is -- the whole function: vacate that one. A frame in no seat at all was never this manager's -- to place, so it is simply hidden. function HideUIPanel(frame) if not frame or not frame:IsShown() then return end
if frame == GetFullScreenFrame() then SetFullScreenFrame(nil) elseif frame == GetCenterFrame() then SetCenterFrame(nil) elseif frame == GetLeftFrame() then -- l.777-782: a LEFT-area panel parked at center (it was pushed there) slides back -- into the seat we are giving up, rather than being stranded beside an empty left -- slot. A native-center frame stays where it is. if AreaOf(GetCenterFrame()) == "left" then MovePanelToLeft() else SetLeftFrame(nil) end else -- Seated nowhere: a plain toplevel, or an addon's frame we never placed. frame:Hide() end end
-- UISpecialFrames (UIParent.lua l.52-55) — **the addon's own ESC list**, and the reason -- this stopped being "dropped: none exist yet" (decision 1206). -- -- `tinsert(UISpecialFrames, "MyFrame")` is THE 1.12 idiom for "ESC should close my -- window", and it is 34 call sites across the corpus. With the table absent that line is -- `bad argument #1 to 'tinsert' (table expected, got nil)` — which killed 11 addons at -- load, the second-largest wall in the survey after the Lua-5.0 generic-for. -- -- Seeded with the reference's own two entries — **both** of them now. 1206 seeded only -- `ItemRefTooltip`, and its Rejected section wrote down why, verbatim: *"Listing -- `ColorPickerFrame`. The reference seeds it; we do not ship one, and a name that resolves -- to nothing is skipped harmlessly — but seeding a frame we lack would be writing a claim -- we cannot honour."* ColorPickerFrame.xml ships it, so the claim is honourable now, and -- the entry is the reference's own rather than one of ours. -- -- Note it does NOT contradict the paragraph above (our own escapable toplevels stay -- hard-listed in the ESC chain). The concern there is an addon's `tremove` breaking the -- CLIENT's own ESC; here the ESC chain carries the colour picker on its own rung — and has -- to, because ESC on this window must CANCEL (restore the colour), which this walk's plain -- `Hide` cannot do. So the table entry is not what makes ESC work; it is what makes -- `CloseWindows` put the picker away when something ELSE closes the world's windows — -- opening the game menu, a `CloseAllWindows()` — which is exactly the reference's own -- behaviour on that path, cancel-less Hide and all. UISpecialFrames = { "ItemRefTooltip", "ColorPickerFrame" }
-- CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) — UIParent.lua l.928-957. Both once-dropped slices are now -- carried: the UISpecialFrames loop at l.947-954, and the doublewide seat (decision 1511). function CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) local fullScreenFrame = GetFullScreenFrame() local doublewideFrame = GetDoublewideFrame() local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() local leftFrame = GetLeftFrame()
HideUIPanel(leftFrame) HideUIPanel(fullScreenFrame) -- l.938. HideUIPanel has no doublewide branch, so this lands on its "seated nowhere" -- arm and is a plain Hide; the seat itself is never vacated (SetDoublewideFrame's note). HideUIPanel(doublewideFrame) -- l.934, quoted as-is: `found` deliberately does NOT consider the doublewide frame, -- even though the line above closes it. Reproduced rather than corrected — ESC's "did -- I close anything?" answer is this value, and changing it would change which key -- press opens the game menu. (Computed off the locals read before any Hide landed.) local found = leftFrame or centerFrame or fullScreenFrame -- `ignoreCenter` spares a NATIVE-center frame and nothing else: a left-area panel -- merely parked at the center seat closes with the rest of them. if centerFrame and not (ignoreCenter and AreaOf(centerFrame) == "center") then HideUIPanel(centerFrame) end
-- The special frames, the reference's own loop (l.947-954): a plain Hide, never -- HideUIPanel, because these hold no panel slot. Its `for index, value in -- UISpecialFrames do` is Lua 5.0's iterator-less generic-for, which our VM cannot run -- (decision 1202) — `ipairs` is the same walk in the dialect we have. for _, name in ipairs(UISpecialFrames) do local frame = getglobal(name) if frame and frame:IsVisible() then frame:Hide() found = 1 end end
return found end
-- CloseAllWindows(ignoreCenter) — UIParent.lua l.970-982. The real fn first loops -- ContainerFrame1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES to hide any open bags, then calls CloseWindows() for -- the panel slots, returning whether anything closed. benilla ships a single backpack window -- (BenillaBagFrame, decision 0068 T2), so that loop collapses to hiding it. "Text") local sideWidths = 2 * getglobal(name .. "Left"):GetWidth() local width, tabWidth if absoluteSize then if absoluteSize < sideWidths then width, tabWidth = 1, sideWidths else width, tabWidth = absoluteSize - sideWidths, absoluteSize end text:SetWidth(width) else width = text:GetStringWidth() + (padding or 24) if maxWidth and width > maxWidth then width = maxWidth + (padding or 24) text:SetWidth(width) else text:SetWidth(0) end tabWidth = width + sideWidths end getglobal(name .. "Middle"):SetWidth(width) getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):SetWidth(width) tab:SetWidth(tabWidth) -- benilla addition: hand back the width just declared. `tab:GetWidth()` cannot serve -- it — that reads the last RESOLVED rect, which inside a settle is this frame's stale -- input, not the value one line above just set. A clamp that read it back saw the old -- width, declined to fire, and the settle's gate then locked the un-clamped result in -- for good (decision 1002). return tabWidth end
-- The tab template's per-frame settle: the ref does TabResize(0) once, in OnShow -- (CharacterFrameTemplates.xml l.77-80), trusting a synchronous text measure. Our -- GetStringWidth has a frame of latency, so the template's OnUpdate calls this until the -- measured width settles (then it's a no-op compare per frame). The ref sizes the hover -- highlight alongside it; this kit does not — both tab templates anchor their highlight to -- their own side edges, so it is the tab by construction and no settle can desync it -- (decision 1004). -- -- The fit PARAMETERS live on the tab (`benillaTabPadding`/`benillaTabMaxWidth`, defaulting -- to the +0 fit every window tab has always used) rather than at the call site, because -- there is exactly one call site and it is this settle loop: an instance that ran its own -- TabResize in OnLoad — as the reference's macro tabs do — would just be overwritten on the -- next frame. Setting the two fields IS how an instance asks for the reference's own fit. -- THE STRUCTURAL CLAMP — a tab may never grow past its window's drawn right edge, whatever -- the instance asked for (decision 1002; the director's "fix this properly to prevent it -- ever again"). The reference's own caps are numbers hand-tuned to ITS font: the macro -- window's 150 is right for the enUS FRIZQT__ the 1.12 client rasterizes and for nothing -- else in particular, and the label it guards carries a CHARACTER NAME — the one string -- whose width no window author can know. So the instance's cap is a preference and the -- window's edge is the law. -- -- `benillaTabRightInset` is how a window declares how far its DRAWN plate stops short of -- its frame rect, because no kit can introspect an art margin. The macro window's is 40: -- its 384-unit frame is painted by a 256-wide slice plus a 128-wide one that carries a -- transparent tail. Clamping to the frame rect instead — the first attempt — clamped to a -- boundary the player cannot see, and the tab still walked out over the world. -- -- The clamp is applied to the RESULT, through TabResize's own `absoluteSize` arm, rather -- than folded into `maxWidth`: that parameter is compared against `text + padding` but -- assigned as `maxWidth + padding`, so a room budget expressed through it is off by the -- padding and silently fails to bind. `absoluteSize` sets the tab width outright, which is -- exactly what a room budget is. function BenillaTab_Room(tab) local parent = tab:GetParent() if not parent then return nil end local left, right = tab:GetLeft(), parent:GetRight() if not left or not right then return nil end local room = (right - (tab.benillaTabRightInset or 0)) - left if room < 1 then room = 1 end return room end
